description: Site: oscal/emit.rs:619-632. scope_text returns &str (empty string fallback); scope_bytes returns &[u8] (empty slice fallback). Comment says: 'Used by encode_scope for canonical kinds whose schema is enforced by constructors (so missing/wrong-typed props indicate a code-side bug, not caller misuse).' That's an internal-invariant claim, but the public DeviationScope::props is a Vec<(String, ScopePropValue)> that any caller can construct directly via struct literal (kind and props are pub). When a hand-constructed scope is missing the prop, encode_scope emits an OSCAL Subject with an empty title field ('Issuer DN contains \'\'') and empty props. The Risk emitter then produces a JSON document that is structurally valid but semantically meaningless. Cleaner: scope_text/scope_bytes return Option, and encode_scope returns Result<Vec<Value>, EncodeError>; the call site in risk_for_deviation propagates the error. Or: validate at DeviationScope construction time that the expected props for the kind are present (already done in constructors, but not for direct struct literals). The current shape silently produces a non-round-trippable OSCAL artifact for an invariant-breaking scope, which is a debugging-time tax.
title: scope_text / scope_bytes silently return empty defaults instead of returning Option
